# micromdm: twenty-seven quiet misbehaviours, reported without a test suite

We took a fresh checkout of this management system together with the small tool that drives it and exercised it the way we normally do, and an alarming number of unrelated things now come back wrong. The repository has received 27 separate undocumented edits. Nothing crashes on startup, so each problem has to be found from what it does.

Asking over the HTTP interface for a managed machine to be told to do something goes wrong in several independent ways. If we attach our own identifier to the request, it is thrown away and a generated one is used instead; if we attach an identifier that is empty or nothing but blanks, that blank value is kept verbatim rather than being replaced by a generated one — the inverse of what we want in both cases. A request to adjust a setting whose item carries only a number, such as a software-update recommendation cadence of zero, can no longer be encoded at all: the encoder errors out and nothing is produced. A settings item carrying an embedded dictionary of application preferences still encodes, and the keys inside it still arrive intact.

Sending out a company-built application package with its accompanying inventory attached produces something with none of that inventory in it — no bundle identifiers, no versions, no sizes, no titles, no kinds — as though it had never been supplied.
